Smt. Kalibai vs Dulesingh on 6 August, 2025
 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Ind:20919

 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Pavan Kumar Dwivedi

On The 6 th Of August, 2025
 Misc. Appeal No. 2553 of 2024
 Smt. Kalibai And Others
 Versus
 Dulesingh And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Manish Jain - Advocate for the appellants.
 Shri Sudarshan Pandit, learned counsel for the responde
 Order
01.

Heard on I.A.No.7332/2025, an application for dispensation of service on respondents No.1 and 2.
02.

It is submitted that respondents No.1 and 2 are owner and driver of the offending vehicle and their presence is not necessary for a complete and effective adjudication of this appeal which can be decided even in their absence.
03. For the reasons stated in the application, the same is allowed and service of notice upon respondent No.1 and 2 is dispensed with at the risk of the appellants.
0 5 . In view of the order as aforesaid I.A. No.7332/2025 also stands closed.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20919 2 MA-2553-2024 06.
With consent of learned counsel for the parties the matter is finally heard.

07. This appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the appellants / claimants being aggrieved by the award dated 8/1/2024 passed in MACC No.6/2023 by the First Member, Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sardapur, District Dhar whereby a total sum of Rs.12,99,792/- has been awarded to the appellants / claimants by way of compensation.

entities.text: Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Sardapur, District Dhar
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 08. As per the appellants, on 5/11/2022 Nirbhay Singh (the deceased) was going from his motorcycle bearing registration number M.P. - 11 B.C. 3952 from four lane road.

At that time Smt. Kalibai vs Dulesingh on 6 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32665538/
1

respondent No.1 drove the vehicle bearing registration number R.J. 27 G.C. 6213 which was owned by respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed the same from behind into the vehicle of the deceased as a result of which he fell down and suffered grievous injuries on his head.
He was admitted in the hospital, but eventually died during treatment.
09. Thereafter the appellants filed an application under Section 166 of the M.V. Act, 1988 for award of compensation to them on account of his death.
The application was contested by respondent No.3 Insurance Co. by filing its written statement to the same.

Upon evaluation of the evidence brought on record by the parties the claims tribunal has awarded a total compensation of Rs.12,99,792/- out of which amount of Rs.10,23,792/- was for loss of dependency.

10. Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the assessment of NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:20919 3 MA-2553-2024 income by the claims tribunal is not correct.
Resultantly the compensation under the head of loss of dependency also on a lesser side.
He submits that the income of the deceased has been taken incorrectly.

It is the assertion of the counsel for the appellants that deceased Nirbhay Singh was receiving salary of Rs.30,000/- per month as well as a bonus of Rs.5000/- thus a total sum of Rs.35,000/- per month was being earned by the deceased Nirbhay Singh, who was working as a driver.
He submits that there was no reason for claims tribunal to disbelieve this assertion of the appellants.

On perusal of the material available on record,
it is seen that there is no material evidence available for establishing this claim of the appellants.
Witness Virendra (AW.3) has also not produced any material for establishing this claim that the deceased was earning Rs.35,000/- per month.
Thus in the considered view of this Court the claims tribunal has rightly disbelieved the claim of the appellants regarding income of the deceased at Rs.35,000/- per month.

However, it is seen that while taking the income of the deceased on notional basis at Rs.6500/- by treating him an unskilled labour, no reference has been made by the claims tribunal to any material so as to arrive at this conclusion.
The date of accident is 5/11/2022.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Hans Raj V/s. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd passed in SLP(C)
No.3511 of 2020 has held that in absence of any material to ascertain income of the deceased /
injured support of the guidelines issued by the State Legal Services Authority can be taken.

entities.text: Hans Raj V/s. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 11 . On perusal of the guidelines for the relevant period, it is seen that minimum wages for an unskilled labour at relevant point of time was Rs.9,335/-.
Thus the same is taken as the income of the deceased on the date of accident.
Apart from the income the compensation on all other heads has properly been NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:20919 4 MA-2553-2024 awarded by the claims tribunal.
Thus only modification is to be done for assessment of the compensation for loss of dependency in view of the income as determined hereinabove.
12. After the above modification in the income the compensation for loss of dependency would come to Rs.14,68,687/- and the total of compensation would come to Rs.17,44,687.50/-.
After deducting the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal at Rs.12,99,792/-, the appellants are now entitled for compensation of Rs.4,44,895.50/-, which is rounded as Rs.4,45,000/-.
